‘Wouldn’t you?’: Bonnie Blue claims new baby will be named after betting company

Rage-bait pornstar Bonnie Blue revealed her baby’s bizarre name after auctioning off naming rights for an outrageous sum.

Bianca Soldani
2 min read
September 24, 2026 - 12:05PM
news.com.au
Bonnie Blue says she thinks 'thoroughly about what I’m going to do'

Bonnie Blue has apparently settled on a name for her newborn baby, and it’s come with a $2.25 million (£1.2 million) payday.

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:40
Instaread

The 27-year-old took to Instagram on Wednesday to claim she’d named her first born after betting company and ‘crypto casino’ BetBolt, after she auctioned off the chance to pick the baby’s moniker to the highest bidder.

“I’m going to be shouting BetBolt across the playground,” she told her followers.

Other top contenders for the name were “Top G” and “Group Project”, with Blue saying of the latter: “That would’ve been fun, but I do think Social Services would have an issue with that.”

Blue claimed she is going to make the name official tomorrow and already has an appointment at the registry office.

Despite threatening to do so, it’s unclear whether Blue will actually attempt to legally name her child after the Union of Comoros-based company, or more likely, only refer to them by that title on her platforms.

The UK doesn’t have restrictions on baby names, however names that are likely to subject a child to ridicule, or that mimic legally recognised titles like “Prince” or “Lady” are routinely knocked back.

Anticipating that people would call the move “disgusting or rage bait”, she asked, “wouldn’t you for £1.2 million rename your kid? I know I would.”

The sex worker, whose business model relies on increasingly outrageous stunts to stoke engagement and drive clicks, got the reception she expected with people replying “great mother” and “I feel bad for the baby”.

One person on Instagram claimed the post should have been labelled as sponsored content “because that’s clearly what this is. Advertising standards authority should be notified”.

This latest outrage comes after Blue was reported to Britain’s National Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Children charity (NSPCC) for a social media video promoting her OnlyFans.

The video featured her sitting on a bed holding her weeks-old baby while surrounded by men in balaclavas.

“Yes I just had a baby,” she said, “But that means the six week rule does not apply to me because I had a C-section. Down there still looking perfect.”

She said when a baby’s safety is at stake, looking away is “not an option”.

“Children are not adults. They must never be involved in pornography, used to promote adult entertainment, or absorbed into a parent’s sexualised commercial brand,” she wrote.

“Even the suggestion that a child may be placed in such circumstances is deeply disturbing.”
